issues.description: Image bytes pushed downstream without colour-space conversion; postcondition violated
issues.detail: The code opens the inline data with PIL and pushes `image.tobytes()` declaring `format="RGB"`. There is no precondition that the inline data is in any particular mode — Gemini image responses are typically PNG/JPEG which PIL decodes into modes such as RGBA, P, or L depending on source. `tobytes()` returns the raw buffer of whatever mode the image is in, not RGB. The downstream consumer is told it is receiving RGB pixel data of `image.size` bytes; this is a lie when the mode is not RGB. The correct discipline is `image.convert("RGB").tobytes()` (or `RGBA` with declared format), so the asserted postcondition matches the produced bytes.

issues.description: Module-level mutation of a private SDK attribute is a smuggled goto into another library's state
issues.detail: `genai._api_client.READ_BUFFER_SIZE = 5 * 1024 * 1024`, executed unconditionally at import time inside a `try` block, mutates a private attribute of a third-party module as a side effect of importing this file. The author admits it is a "temporary hack." The precondition (that `_api_client` exposes this name and that 5 MiB is sufficient) is undocumented; there is no postcondition check, no fallback, and no version guard. Any future google-genai release that renames or removes the attribute will raise `AttributeError` at import and break every Google service in pipecat, not merely image generation. This is the textbook case of managing complexity by reaching across an abstraction boundary and hoping.

issues.description: Silent default-model change is an undocumented behavioural break
issues.detail: The constructor default moves from `gemini-2.0-flash` to `gemini-2.5-flash`. Existing callers who relied on the default now silently get a different model with different latency, cost, token accounting, and thinking-budget semantics. The CHANGELOG entry under "Changed" notes the model change but says nothing of the implicit thinking-budget behaviour invoked by `_maybe_unset_thinking_budget`. Callers who did not opt in have had their preconditions altered without notice.

issues.description: Image-model detection uses substring match on model name — fragile guard
issues.detail: `if "image" in self._model_name` is a string-contains test masquerading as a predicate. The invariant the author intends is "this model returns inline image data and does not support a thinking budget," but the test will match any future model whose name happens to contain the substring `image` for any reason (e.g. `gemini-2.6-pro-imagen-eval`). The discipline is to maintain an explicit allowlist of image-capable model identifiers, or query a capability, not to pattern-match on marketing names.

issues.description: No handling of the negative branches: image decode failure, empty buffer, oversized image
issues.detail: The new `elif part.inline_data and part.inline_data.data:` branch assumes the bytes are a decodable image of bounded size. There is no try/except around `Image.open`; a malformed payload from the upstream model raises `PIL.UnidentifiedImageError` and propagates through `_process_context`, aborting the whole turn. There is no size cap to defend against the 5 MiB hack being insufficient. The author has reasoned about the happy path only. State the postcondition under failure and handle it, or document that failure is fatal by design.

issues.description: Dependency range widened from compatible-release to `>=x,<major+1` without justification
issues.detail: `google-genai` moves from `~=1.24.0` to `>=1.41.0,<2`, and similarly for the speech/tts packages. Compatible-release (`~=`) was the prior invariant; the new range admits any 1.x release including unreleased ones. There is no statement of which API surface is depended on, so the upper bound is effectively `<2` by hope. If the only reason for the bump is `_api_client.READ_BUFFER_SIZE` and the new image part shape, pin closer to what was actually tested.

issues.description: Stray blank line inserted with no semantic content
issues.detail: An empty line is added between `self._http_options = http_options` and `self._create_client(...)`. The diff records a change of nothing. Either the cosmetic edit was unintentional, or it is a marker of a removed line during development. Either way, churn without reasoning.

issues.description: No test accompanies the new control-flow branch
issues.detail: A new `elif` arm has been added in the candidate-part loop and a new branch in `_maybe_unset_thinking_budget`. The PR contains an example script but no unit test exercising either branch with a synthetic candidate containing `inline_data`. "Testing shows the presence of bugs, not their absence" — but the absence of testing shows neither, and here it shows the author has not even attempted to demonstrate the postcondition holds on a controlled input.

review.summary: The change is UNREASONED and contains a SMUGGLED-GOTO into a third-party library's private state. Two P0 defects: the mutation of `genai._api_client.READ_BUFFER_SIZE` at import time is a temporary hack that will break every Google service when the underlying attribute moves, and the new image branch pushes `image.tobytes()` while declaring `format=\"RGB\"` without any colour-space conversion, so the produced bytes do not satisfy the asserted postcondition for non-RGB source images. The author has not stated the precondition for `part.inline_data` (mode, decodability, bounded size), nor handled its negation. The substring guard `\"image\" in self._model_name` is a string heuristic where an explicit capability predicate is required. REFUSED in its present form; the path to acceptance is removing the global mutation, converting pixel data to a declared mode, and stating and testing the invariant for the inline-data branch.
